en: “Giving gifts to those who are unworthy, yet not bestowing them upon those worthy to receive;”
One who has fallen into calamity finds no companion;
nor does one who gives gifts to unworthy recipients [find a friend].
He who bestows gifts upon those worthy of them finds a companion when he falls into misfortune.
The display of association and shared enjoyment with those who are ignoble,
whereas that which is done for the noble ones, who are upright, endures.
Even a tiny deed toward such as these bears great fruit.
He who has previously performed wholesome deeds performs what is very difficult to do in this world.
Whether he should act later or not,
he is worthy of ultimate honor.
Thus ends the second Jātaka, the Mahāassāroha Jātaka.
